what_happened: Main Migration Event 20-22 Apr 2018 moved corporate systems, services and customer data of ~5.2m customers to a newly built platform; digital, telephone and branch services failed; BAU not restored until 10 Dec 2018.
root_causes: Unproven newly built platform; testing compressed, run in parallel and descoped (Active-Active) to meet dates; no dedicated performance environment (per report coverage); outsourcer with no experience operating the platform and 85 fourth parties; readiness attestations not challenged; largely single-event migration chosen without sufficient consideration.
cost_or_impact: £48.65m FCA/PRA penalties (2022); £32.7m redress; 225,492 complaints (c.4.3% of customers); individual CIO penalty by PRA (2023).
lesson: Data migrated successfully yet the migration failed: operational readiness (capacity, config parity, supplier capability) is part of migration acceptance. Schedule pressure that compresses testing is the leading indicator.

case: Revlon SAP ERP go-live at Oxford, North Carolina
what_happened: ERP launch disrupted manufacturing and shipping; customer service levels fell.
root_causes: Insufficient risk assessment of the implementation; process-level controls did not reliably record inventory, receivables, sales and COGS (per auditor report summary); limited trained staff.
cost_or_impact: ~$64m net sales not shipped in 2018; $53.6m incremental charges; material weakness in ICFR disclosed; shares fell >10% after hours (press).
lesson: A platform change can break financial controls even when the system runs; control design and staff training are migration deliverables, and control-effectiveness evidence must exist from day one.

what_happened: Seven-year programme piloted in some countries then halted in 2018; Lidl reverted to its legacy system.
root_causes: Domain-model mismatch: Lidl values inventory at purchase price while SAP for Retail defaults to retail-price valuation; heavy adaptation of standard software (press analysis).
cost_or_impact: ~€500m estimated (press; unconfirmed by Lidl or SAP).
lesson: Where a customer's core accounting semantics differ from the product's, conversion becomes customization. Unbound must decide up front which sponsor accounting semantics it supports natively (unitization vs. balance, fee bases, valuation timing) and reject the rest at sales time.

what_happened: New payroll went live March 2010; widespread under/over/non-payment of health staff; Commission of Inquiry reported July 2013.
root_causes: Go-live despite known defects; parallel pay run recommended by vendor largely not followed (Auditor-General, per press); complex award interpretation; disputed data-migration and business-process issues; weak state governance.
cost_or_impact: ~A$1.25bn cited by press for total cost of system and remediation.
lesson: Calculation-heavy migrations (pay, fees, unit values) need shadow comparison of outputs against legacy for full periods before cutover; go-live decisions need hard exit criteria.

what_happened: State exchange never launched online enrollment as designed; state moved to the federal platform.
root_causes: No independent systems integrator; state largely dependent on vendor; unrealistic expectations; vendor and state blame each other (contested).
cost_or_impact: ~$300m federal funds spent overall per press; ~$132-134m paid to Oracle per AP (press).
lesson: Vendor-dependent delivery without an independent integration authority shifts risk to the buyer. For Unbound: the sponsor must be able to verify migration results with its own tools (reconciliation reports reproducible by the sponsor), not take the vendor's word.

case: AEF DonorCentral to Ren platform change (DAF)
what_happened: AEF moved to Ren (selected Jul 2025, fully on Ren Apr 2026, old portal retired 31 Oct 2026); 33 months of history imported but the new portal exposes two years; older records by staff request. Only national-sponsor case found; community-foundation cases are in draft 10.
root_causes: History not carried into self-service; cause not publicly documented (scope choice, cost or data format unknown).
cost_or_impact: Donor self-service history discontinuity; no cost, downtime or attrition figures public.
lesson: The DAF-specific failure mode is degraded donor history, not outage. CNV-EXP-002 differentiates only as a published, verifiable outcome (history depth, reconciliation proof), since incumbents also sell migration services; source-limited history must be disclosed as HISTORY_GAP.

what_happened: EUR344m impairment of legacy systems at programme start (2014); phased product/country migrations (e.g. ~250,000 Finnish savings accounts Apr 2018); 2021 press reports slow progress.
root_causes: Not publicly documented with primary evidence; multi-country, multi-legacy (Midas, Tieto) scope.
cost_or_impact: Programme cost and final outcome not established from sources read.
lesson: Partial/uncertain case: phased migration lowers blast radius but can extend programmes for years; Unbound waves should have a fixed end condition per sponsor.
